name: Call of Water
summary: Brine's water reaches Islen Waterseer on the eastern Barrens coast, where the next part of the shamanic trial begins. The vial holds water Brine prepared and blessed, the base for a sapta that lets an initiate see water spirits in Silverpine Forest.

sections.title: Return to the Shore
sections.body: After the trials in the southern Barrens, Brine gives the shaman initiate a Vial of Purest Water. The water comes from pure springs and has been consecrated by Brine's rites. The initiate carries it back to the eastern coast, where Islen Waterseer keeps watch. The water links Brine's teachings with the rites of the totem.

sections.title: The Purpose of the Sapta
sections.body: Islen explains that mortal eyes cannot easily see water spirits. To meet them, an initiate drinks a brew called a sapta. The water from Brine will form the base of that draught and open the shaman's senses to what ordinary sight cannot find. Seeing the spirits is only part of the journey; they will test the initiate.

sections.title: A Crossing to Lordaeron
sections.body: Islen sends the shaman beyond Kalimdor, across the sea to Silverpine Forest, south of the Undercity. Beside an isolated shrine, the initiate must drink the sapta and face the elementals directly. Only then can the shaman earn the right to manifest the Water Totem.

faq.q: What is inside the Vial of Purest Water?
faq.answer: The Vial of Purest Water holds water gathered from pure springs and consecrated by Brine's rites. It is the essential base for brewing a sapta, which lets a shaman communicate with water spirits.
Islen Waterseer is an elder shaman who lives on the Barrens' secluded southeastern coast, south of Ratchet. She mentors Horde shamans seeking communion with water and the Water Totem.
A sapta is a ceremonial drink prepared by shamanic mentors. It changes a shaman's perception, allowing them to see and meet elemental spirits hidden from mortal sight.

faq.q: Why do I have to go to Silverpine Forest next?
faq.answer: The shrine for this communion lies in Silverpine Forest's coastal waters, south of the Undercity in the Eastern Kingdoms. The spirits there require a shaman to meet them and face a final trial before gaining mastery over water.
Brine lives in a secluded hut in the southern Barrens, high in the hills west of the road toward the Great Lift and Thousand Needles.

faq.q: Can any shaman bypass making the sapta?
faq.answer: No. The communion rites require a shaman's spirit to be attuned to the unseen world. Without a sapta to open that way, the water spirits at the shrine cannot be met or challenged.

angles.text: As a Horde shaman, you complete the Call of Water rites to commune with the spirits and earn the Water Totem, which governs healing and replenishment.
As a member of the Horde, you travel from the Barrens in Kalimdor to Silverpine in Lordaeron, crossing lands held by the Forsaken as you undertake the trial.
